_about: Curated year-by-year supplement written for GeoHistory from general knowledge (conservative: well-established dates only). Each entry names the English Wikipedia article it is about; tools/build_curated.py sets "verified" when the Wikidata item of that article carries the same year. Places are approximate (nearest town).
period: Fall of the Roman Republic, 133 to 27 BC

events.label: Tiberius Gracchus is tribune and is killed
events.desc: Tiberius Gracchus pushes a land reform as tribune of the plebs and is killed by senators and their followers in Rome.

events.label: Gaius Gracchus is tribune
events.desc: Gaius Gracchus, brother of Tiberius, becomes tribune and proposes wider reforms; he dies in 121 BC.

events.label: Gaius Marius is consul for the first time
events.desc: Marius is elected consul and takes command of the war against Jugurtha in Numidia.

events.label: Social War begins
events.desc: Rome's Italian allies revolt after being refused citizenship; most receive it by the end of the war.

events.label: Sulla marches on Rome
events.desc: Sulla leads his legions into Rome, the first Roman general to take the city by force.

events.label: Sulla becomes dictator
events.desc: After winning the civil war Sulla is made dictator and orders the proscriptions.

events.label: Third Servile War begins
events.desc: Gladiators led by Spartacus break out of a school at Capua; the slave revolt is crushed in 71 BC.

events.label: Catilinarian conspiracy
events.desc: The consul Cicero exposes Catiline's plot to seize power in Rome.

events.label: First Triumvirate formed
events.desc: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus make an informal alliance to dominate Roman politics.

events.label: Gallic Wars begin
events.desc: Caesar begins the campaigns that bring Gaul under Roman rule by 50 BC.

events.label: Battle of Carrhae
events.desc: The Parthians destroy a Roman army; Crassus is killed.

events.label: Battle of Alesia
events.desc: Caesar besieges and defeats Vercingetorix, ending large-scale Gallic resistance.

events.label: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.desc: Caesar leads a legion across the Rubicon into Italy, starting the civil war against Pompey and the Senate.

events.label: Battle of Pharsalus
events.desc: Caesar defeats Pompey in Thessaly; Pompey flees to Egypt and is killed there.

events.label: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.desc: Caesar, dictator for life, is stabbed to death by senators on the Ides of March.

events.label: Second Triumvirate formed
events.desc: Octavian, Mark Antony and Lepidus take power by law and proscribe their enemies; Cicero is killed.

events.label: Battle of Philippi
events.desc: Antony and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius in Macedonia.

events.label: Battle of Actium
events.desc: Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeats Antony and Cleopatra off western Greece.

events.label: Egypt becomes a Roman province
events.desc: After the deaths of Antony and Cleopatra, Octavian annexes Egypt.

events.label: Octavian receives the name Augustus
events.desc: The Senate grants Octavian the name Augustus; the date is usually taken as the start of the Roman Empire.
